product.title: Deal Dynasty — Business Strategy Game
product.summary: Seven rounds, each teaching a different negotiation or game-theory idea.
product.whatStudentsDo: Students pitch investors under signalling pressure, weigh competing offers against their walk-away, buy from a seller who knows more than they do, run a five-week pricing standoff with a rival, build a reputation, make a credible commitment, and close a three-party deal needing two of three to agree.

studentDataProfile.notes: State kept in browser localStorage only; no server call observed.

governance.maturityBasis: Complete and publicly reachable, with an explicit teaching note closing each round. No student-run evidence exists.

health.technicalBasis: Playtested end to end 2026-08-16. Seven rounds covering signalling, BATNA, information asymmetry, repeated games and multi-party bargaining, with vivid scenario writing and feedback that explains why an option worked. A repeated pricing game iterates against a tit-for-tat rival, and squeezing an ally in the three-party round genuinely collapses the deal.
knownBlockers: Reputation carries no weight at the ending. A deliberately greedy, dishonest run finished with MORE cash than an honest one ($43,000 against $41,000) despite reputation of 32 against 71, and both received the identical title "Savvy Dealmaker".
The Round Breakdown list on the results screen prints every row twice.

curation.tierBasis: Signalling, BATNA, repeated games and multi-party bargaining in one coherent arc, with feedback that explains why an option failed. Reputation currently carries no weight at the ending.

provenance.evidence: 301-M3-ECON/index.html subtitle 'Build your business empire in 7 high-stakes rounds'; each round object carries concept and teach fields covering signalling and screening, BATNA, information asymmetry, repeated games, reputation, commitment devices and multi-party bargaining.
